data.title: Backtrack
data.solution:
s = input().strip()
n = int(input())

operations = []

for _ in range(n):
    operations.append(input().strip())

for op in reversed(operations):

    if op == "R":
        s = s[::-1]

    elif op[0] == "L":
        k = int(op[1:])
        k %= len(s)
        s = s[-k:] + s[:-k]

    elif op[0] == "B":
        k = int(op[1:])
        result = []

        for i in range(0, len(s), k):
            block = s[i:i + k]

            if len(block) == k:
                block = block[::-1]

            result.append(block)

        s = "".join(result)

    elif op[0] == "X":
        k = int(op[1:])
        opposite = len(s) - 1 - k

        chars = list(s)
        chars[k], chars[opposite] = chars[opposite], chars[k]
        s = "".join(chars)

print(s)
data.statement:
<<This clash is in Reverse mode only.>>

A machine transforms a string by applying a sequence of operations.

Given a transformed string and the operations in the order they were performed, recover the original string.

The operations are:

<<R>>: reverses the entire string.
<<Lk>>: moves the first <<k>> characters to the end of the string.
<<Bk>>: divides the string into blocks of <<k>> characters and reverses each complete block. A final incomplete block is left unchanged.
<<Xk>>: swaps the character at position <<k>> with the character at the opposite position.

Positions start at 0.

The operations are given in the order in which they were originally performed.

Goal

This clash is in Reverse mode only.

A machine transforms a string by applying a sequence of operations.

Given a transformed string and the operations in the order they were performed, recover the original string.

The operations are:

R: reverses the entire string.
Lk: moves the first k characters to the end of the string.
Bk: divides the string into blocks of k characters and reverses each complete block. A final incomplete block is left unchanged.
Xk: swaps the character at position k with the character at the opposite position.

Positions start at 0.

The operations are given in the order in which they were originally performed.
Input
Line 1: A string s, representing the string after all operations have been performed.
Line 2: An integer n, representing the number of operations.
Next n lines: One operation per line.

Each operation is one of:

R
Lk, where k is the number of positions to rotate.
Bk, where k is the block size.
Xk, where k is a character position.
Output
Line 1: The original string s, before any operation was performed.
Constraints
1 <= length of s <= 20
1 <= n <= 20
1 <= k < length of s for Lk and Bk
0 <= k < length of s for Xk
s only contains alphabetical characters.
Example
Input
dfbace
3

L2
X1

abcdef
